title: Transgenic Animals

visualization.desc: A transgenic animal carries a foreign gene inside the same double helix as its own DNA.

notes: A transgenic animal carries a gene that came from another organism, and that gene is present in the animal's cells and is expressed. The gene is extra DNA, not a temporary injection of protein.

The usual route in mice starts with a fertilised egg. Copies of the foreign DNA are microinjected into one pronucleus. The egg is placed in a surrogate mother. Offspring are then tested to see which ones actually incorporated the gene.

Only some injected eggs take up the DNA, and only some of those pass the gene on. Screening, often with a marker or by looking for the DNA itself, is part of the method. An animal that merely received a protein is not transgenic.

The inserted gene must be expressed, not just sit in the genome. A promoter that works in the host decides where and when the new protein is made. A gene without a working promoter does not change the animal's phenotype.

Mice are the common first host because they breed quickly and their embryos are well studied. The same idea has been used in fish, pigs, sheep and cattle when a product or a disease model is wanted in that species.

Making the animal is only the first half of the topic. The reason for doing it — disease models, proteins in milk, and safety tests — belongs with the uses. The method here is the transfer of a chosen gene into the germline so every cell of the offspring can carry it.
confusion: A transgenic animal is not any animal that has been cloned. Cloning copies a genome. Transgenesis adds a foreign gene.
Injecting a hormone into an adult does not make that adult transgenic. The gene has to be in the DNA.
Not every offspring of an injected egg carries the new gene. The litter has to be screened.
The foreign gene is not automatically expressed in every tissue. Expression follows the promoter attached to it.
keyPoints: Transgenic means a foreign gene is in the genome and is expressed.
Microinjection into a fertilised-egg pronucleus is the standard mouse method.
The embryo is carried by a surrogate, then the young are screened.
A promoter controls whether the new gene is actually used.
Cloning and transgenesis are different operations.
importantStatements: The defining feature is an inherited, expressed foreign gene, not a one-off treatment.
Most injected embryos do not become transgenic founders. Screening is required.
The gene is introduced at the start of development so it can be in the germline.
examples: A mouse embryo is injected with a human disease gene so the adult mouse develops a version of that disease for study.
A growth-hormone gene placed in a fish embryo can produce a line that grows faster than its unmodified relatives.
A gene for a human milk protein, joined to a mammary promoter, is aimed at expression in the milk of a transgenic cow rather than in every organ.
universalFacts: The foreign DNA is inserted into a very early embryo so that, if it integrates, daughter cells inherit it.
Expression depends on a promoter the host cell recognises. The coding sequence alone is not enough.
formulas: Path: foreign gene + promoter → microinjection into pronucleus → surrogate → screen offspring → transgenic line.
Transgenic means integrated foreign DNA that is expressed. A protein injection does not qualify.
practice: List the steps from a DNA sample to a screened transgenic mouse.
Explain why a mammary promoter is chosen when the product is wanted in milk.
Say how a clone and a transgenic animal differ.
practiceQuestions: Why are not all pups from an injected egg transgenic?
What does the promoter contribute that the coding sequence does not?
At what stage of the life cycle is the foreign DNA usually introduced, and why?
examNotes: Define transgenic before you describe the injection. The definition is the foreign gene plus its expression.
Name the pronucleus injection and the need to screen. Both are expected in a method answer.
examShortTricks: If the question says 'expressed', mention the promoter, not only the injection.
specialNotes: Write 'fertilised egg' or 'early embryo', not 'the adult is injected with DNA'.
Keep the method in this note and the five uses in the applications note so the two answers do not collapse into one.
importantNotes: Integration is not guaranteed. Say that screening follows birth.
Germline presence is what lets the gene pass to the next generation.

mcs.question: A transgenic animal is one that
options: Has been given a protein injection
Carries and expresses a foreign gene
Is a clone of its parent
Has no nucleus

mcs.question: In mice the foreign DNA is commonly injected into
options: The adult liver
A pronucleus of the fertilised egg
The milk
The bacterial plasmid only

mcs.question: A promoter is added to the foreign gene so that
options: The gene is cut into fragments
The host can transcribe it in the chosen tissue
The animal becomes a clone
Restriction enzymes are unnecessary

mcs.question: Offspring of an injected egg
options: Always carry the new gene
Must be screened, because many do not
Are bacteria
Lose the gene before birth in every case

importantTasks: Write the five-step path from DNA to a transgenic line.
Explain why the gene is put into the embryo rather than the adult.

exercises.question: A student says a mouse is transgenic because it was injected with human insulin. Correct that claim in steps.
steps: A protein injection does not change the mouse genome.
A transgenic mouse must carry the foreign DNA in its cells.
That DNA is introduced into a fertilised egg, not given as a drug to the adult.
The gene must also be expressed, which needs a working promoter.
exercises.answer: The mouse is transgenic only if the foreign gene is in its DNA and is expressed. An insulin injection is a treatment, not transgenesis.

summary: A transgenic animal is produced by putting a foreign gene into an early embryo, usually by microinjection into a fertilised-egg pronucleus, then screening the offspring for integration and expression. A promoter decides where the gene is used. Cloning copies a genome and is a different procedure.
